title: Perifusion of kidney tissues - Amino acid (AA) vs. AA and hydrogen peroxide treatment for evaluation of oxidative stress
projectDescription: To study longitudinal metabolism in living kidney tissue with an ex vivo platform under defined stimuli
sampleProcessingProtocol: Mouse kidneys were decapsulated and cut into thin axial slices with digestion in control buffer containing 1mg collagenase II (Gibco, MT, USA) per mL on a Thermomixer (Eppendorf, Germany) with 850rpm. Tubules generated were taken from the shaking tube and washed twice in ice-cold control buffer containing an additional 0.5mg albumin/mL. Tubules from four rounds of shaking (first 12min, followed by 5min each) were collected and resuspended in control buffer after sedimentation on ice for distribution into the perifusion chambers.   The tissue pellets from the intracellular metabolite extractions were resuspended in 50µL sodium dodecyl sulfate 4% (SDS) in 50mM HEPES. The samples were cooked at 95°C for 10 minutes. The protein lysate was used in a BCA protein assay (Thermo Fisher Scientific, MA, USA) in a dilution of 1:5 according to the manufacturer’s instruction. Tubular and glomerular protein lysates were substituted to 2.5mM CaCl2 and reduced with 5mM tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine (TCEP) and alkylated with 20mM chloroacetamide (CAA) (10min, 95°C). 30 µg of protein per sample was precipitated to paramagnetic beads for single-pot solid-phase-enhanced sample preparation (SP3) with 80% EtOH. The precleared proteins were digested with trypsin at a 1:50 protease to protein ratio overnight at 37°C. Subsequently, the peptides were purified and enriched using stop-and-go-extraction tips (StageTips).  Samples were separated by an Ultimate 3000 nanoflow-HPLC-MS/MS (Thermo Scientific, MA, USA) coupled to a Quadrupole-Orbitrap Exploris480 mass spectrometer (Thermo Scientific) equipped with a FAIMS  Pro device (High Field Asymmetric Waveform Ion Mobility Spectrometry; standard resolution mode, 3.8 L/min gas flow) operated at alternating compensation voltages of −40 and −61 V. A total of 400ng of peptides was separated using a two-column setup with a PepMap100 C18 trap column (2cm, 75µm ID, 3Å, Thermo Fisher Scientific, MA, USA) and an IonOpticks Gen.2 Aurora 25cm column (IonOpticks, Australia), operated at 50°C, using a 60min gradient. The detailed DIA-MS methodology has been described previously by Demir et al. (PMID:41145914).
dataProcessingProtocol: Analysis for proteome samples was performed with Spectronaut v19.1.240806.62635 (Biognosys) with default settings (directDIA analysis, 1% FDR, no imputation). Trypsin specificity was applied, allowing up to two missed cleavages. Quantification was performed at the MS2 level using fragment ion peak areas with automatic cross-run normalization. The UniProt reference proteome was used (UniProt, 2024-11; 21,757 entries). Carbamidomethylation of cysteine (+57.02146 Da) was set as a fixed modification, while oxidation of methionine (+15.9949 Da) and protein N-terminal acetylation (+42.0210 Da) were set as variable modifications. Data analysis was performed using RStudio (2024.09.0). To reduce the multiple testing burden, statistical analyses were restricted to a predefined set of candidate proteins.
